15-017.r: Nirbhay (tested 7 November 2017, Chandipur) → DRDO's first indigenous long-range subsonic land-attack cruise missile; 300 kg warheads to 1000 km; counter to Pakistan's Babur; not supersonic.

15-018.r: Astra → DRDO's beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile; destroys enemy planes up to 80 km, not 90 km; ballistic test at Chandipur on 20 May 2011.

15-019.r: Astra → India's first indigenous Beyond-Visual-Range air-to-air missile (BVRAAM) by DRDO; engages targets from 20 km up to 80 km.
hi: Air-to-air missile (हवा से हवा में मार करने वाली मिसाइल)

15-021.r: 23 August 2023 → LCA Tejas (LSP-7) test-fired ASTRA, a Beyond Visual Range Air-to-Air Missile, off Goa at about 20,000 feet.

15-022.r: Astra → DRDO air-to-air missile, first successfully tested on 9 May 2003 (Balasore).

15-023.r: Trishul → supersonic short-range missile programme shelved by DRDO in 2008 due to technical flaws.

15-025.r: Nag → shortest range among the options (land version max 4 km); Prithvi-I minimum 150 km; Agni-1 minimum 700 km; Arjun is a battle tank.

15-026.r: Agni → India's intermediate-range surface-to-surface ballistic missile, developed under IGMDP conceived by Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam in the 1980s.

15-027.r: Incorrect: 'A virus cannot reduce pollution' (some viruses help reduce it). True: INFACT-82 naval fast attack craft; Typha computer virus; Brahmos supersonic cruise missile (India–Russia).

15-028.r: Wrong statement: Trishul range 30 km; it was a short-range surface-to-air missile of about 9 km range, shut down in 2008. Other three statements correct.

15-029.r: November 2006 → DRDO interception test used Prithvi-II (interceptor destroyed an 'enemy' Prithvi at 50 km); Prithvi-II (500 kg, 250 km) is not for guarding metros → only 1.

15-030.r: Rafale, MiG-29 and Tejas MK-1 → none is a fifth-generation fighter (fifth generation: stealth, low-probability-of-intercept radar and other advanced technologies).

15-031.r: C-130J Super Hercules (IAF air lifter) → made in the U.S.A. by Lockheed Martin; deal about 1.1 billion dollars, January 2008.

15-032.r: IAF's air-to-air refueller → Ilyushin IL-78, a Soviet four-engined tanker; IAF calls it 'MARS' (Mid-Air Refuelling System).

15-033.r: Dornier-228 → maritime patrol aircraft; C-17 Globemaster III → military transport; IL-76 → strategic heavy-lift transport, not supersonic combat → only two correct.

15-034.r: Sarath (BMP-II) → not an aircraft; Indian version of the Soviet amphibious infantry fighting vehicle BMP-II (1980s). Jaguar, Dornier-228, MiG-27M are aircraft.

15-035.r: Arihant → atomic (nuclear) submarine; Awacs → Israel-developed Falcon for Air Force; Atlas Centaur → American cryogenic rocket (first to use cryogenic engine); Nag → anti-tank missile.

15-036.r: INS Chakra → nuclear-powered Akula-class submarine (8,140 tons) of the Indian Navy, commissioned 4 April 2012.

15-037.r: INS Sindhurakshak → Russian-made diesel-electric submarine of the Indian Navy; sank after a fire at Mumbai naval dockyard on 14 August 2013.

15-038.r: INS Arihant → India's first indigenous (armed) nuclear submarine, inducted August 2016; 83 MW pressurized nuclear reactor; 6000 tons; India 6th nation with nuclear triad.

15-039.r: Agni-I → short-range surface-to-surface ballistic missile; effective range 700–1250 km (above 700 km, below 2000 km).

15-040.r: Agni-I (700 km, nuclear capable) → tested from Wheeler's Island, Odisha on 28 March 2010; first night trial 11 April 2014.

15-041.r: Dhanush → naval version of the Prithvi missile; range 350 km.

15-042.r: Agni-II → range 2000–2500 km (the missile with strike range over 2000 km); Agni-I → 700–1250 km; both from IGMDP.

15-043.r: Hansa-2 → trainer aircraft for flight training, designed by National Aerospace Laboratories (NAL), built by Taneja Aerospace and Aviation Limited.

15-044.r: Wrong pair: Phalcon – Russian cruise missile; Phalcon is an Israeli Airborne Early Warning (AEWC&C) system India bought from Israel. Arjun, Saras, Seabird pairs correct.

15-046.r: Barak anti-missile defence system → bought from Israel; first deployed on aircraft carrier INS Virat.

15-047.r: Barak-8 (Hebrew: Lightning) → India–Israel surface-to-air missile against aircraft, helicopters, anti-ship and cruise missiles, UAVs and jets.

15-048.r: Pilotless (unmanned) helicopter for Indian Navy → developed by Hindustan Aeronautics with Israel Aircraft Industries.

15-049.r: Rafale fighter jets → supplied by French company Dassault Aviation; 36 jets under deal signed 2016, last delivered December 2022.

15-050.r: Arjun → India's modern main battle tank, developed by DRDO with BHEL, BEML and Heavy Vehicles Factory (Tamil Nadu).

15-051.r: First indigenously assembled T-90S battle tank → named 'Bhishma'.

15-052.r: Agni-II → medium-range (2000–2500 km), both stages solid propellant. The 25 January 2002 test at Chandipur was Agni-I (700–1250 km). The book gives no single answer (*).

15-053.r: Agni-II (medium-range, 2000–2500 km) → test-fired from Wheeler's Island near Interim Test Range, Chandipur, Odisha on 17 January 2001; first night trial 16 November 2019.

15-055.r: Agni-IV (earlier Agni-II Prime) → surface-to-surface; two solid stages, not liquid only; 1 tonne warhead to about 4000 km, not 7500 km → only 1.

15-056.r: Agni-V → fully indigenous (so 'not exclusively indigenous' is wrong); range over 5,000 km; about 17 m long, 50 tons; nuclear warhead over one ton.

15-057.r: INDRA → series of 2D radars for Army and Air Force; DRDO's first high-power radar; also used by Sri Lanka.

15-058.r: Prithvi-II → first test-fired 27 January 1996 at Chandipur; single-stage liquid-fuelled; first night test 6 October 2018 by Strategic Forces Command.

15-059.r: Former President Abdul Kalam flew Sukhoi-30 MKI on 8 June 2006; Pratibha Patil flew it on 25 November 2009, first Indian woman in a fighter plane.

15-060.r: May 1992 → USA put a two-year ban on ISRO under the Missile Technology Control Regime.

15-061.r: Founder of India's indigenous missile programme → Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam (IGMDP: Nag, Agni, Prithvi, Trishul, Akash); 11th President of India (2002–2007).
15-061.h: IGMDP missiles 'NAPTA': Nag, Agni, Prithvi, Trishul, Akash.

15-062.r: Shaurya (DRDO, tested 12 November 2008) → short-range canister-launched hypersonic surface-to-surface ballistic missile; range about 700 km with 1000 kg payload, not 900 km.

15-064.r: Shaurya → maximum speed 7.5 Mach (not over 8) and range 700 km (not over 1600 km) → neither statement correct.

15-065.r: Tejas → indigenous 4.5th-generation multi-role Light Combat Aircraft (LCA); named by former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

15-068.r: Tejas → first indigenous fighter plane of IAF; smallest, lightest supersonic multi-role fighter of its class; single-engine tailless delta wing; designed by ADA with HAL.

15-070.r: Admiral Gorshkov → Soviet/Russian aircraft carrier (served 1987–1996); India's $947 million deal (2004) refitted it as INS Vikramaditya, inducted 16 November 2013.

15-071.r: INS Vagir → fifth Scorpene-class submarine, commissioned 23 January 2023 at Mumbai; sixth and last, INS Vaghsheer, on 15 January 2025.

15-072.r: 'Sarthak' → Indian Coast Guard offshore patrol vessel, launched 13 August 2020; built indigenously by Goa Shipyard Limited; 105-metre ship.

15-073.r: 'Vishwast' → first of a new class of offshore patrol vessels by Goa Shipyard; joined the Indian Coast Guard on 17 March 2010.

15-074.r: INS Shakti → fleet tanker built by Italy's Fincantieri (Trieste), not in India; launched 11 October 2010, commissioned 1 October 2011. The book gives no single answer (*).

15-075.r: INS Astradharini → Indian Navy's first fully indigenous torpedo launch and recovery vessel; commissioned at Visakhapatnam on 6 October 2015; 50-metre twin-hulled ship.
